predecessors.name: Rashidun Caliphate
predecessors.text: Syria, which Mu'awiya governed for the Rashidun caliphs from 639, taken out of Ali's caliphate in 656; the rest of the caliphate passed to him in 661

successors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
successors.text: the eastern and central lands taken in the revolution of 747-750: Khorasan, Iran, Iraq, Syria and Egypt

successors.name: Fihrids
successors.text: Ifriqiya, held by the Fihrid emirate

successors.name: Emirate of Córdoba
successors.text: al-Andalus, where the Umayyad prince Abd al-Rahman I 'proclaimed himself emir' in 756

ledger.x: 656: Mu'awiya, governor of Syria, holds Syria against Ali after Uthman's murder.
657: Ali and Mu'awiya fight at Siffin.
658: Mu'awiya annexes Egypt.
660: Busr's raid takes oaths at Medina and Mecca and goes on into Yemen.
660: the two sides stop fighting.
661: Hasan cedes the caliphate and the Hejaz and Yemen fall to Mu'awiya without further fighting: Hasan 'concluded a peace treaty with Mu'awiya', ceding the caliphate.
661: Ali is killed ('In January 661, while praying at the Great Mosque of Kufa') and Hasan, proclaimed at Kufa, cedes the caliphate; Mu'awiya holds the whole of it from 661.
661: Mu'awiya becomes caliph and the Syrian state becomes the Umayyad Caliphate.
661: Damascus becomes the capital.
666-667: Uqba ibn Nafi takes the Fezzan.
670: Uqba ibn Nafi founds Kairouan.
674: Bukhara accepts Arab suzerainty.
683: after Uqba fell at Tahuda near Biskra in 683 'Kusaila now held undisputed mastery over North Africa and marched to Kairouan in triumph'.
683: Ibn al-Zubayr is proclaimed caliph.
Page silent on a date: no page opened says when Arab authority left Armenia and the Caucasus.

Page silent on the date: the Qaysi tribes of northern Syria backed Ibn al-Zubayr while 'central and southern Syria remained loyal to the Umayyads'; placed with the proclamation (683), as zubayrid /ledger/2 does.
Summer 684: Salm appointed Abd Allah ibn Khazim al-Sulami to Khorasan; he 'recognized Ibn al-Zubayr but ruled with virtual independence', a nominal Zubayrid governor 'between 684 and his death'.
Aug 684: Marj Rahit.

Aug 684: after Marj Rahit 'The surviving Qaysis fled to the Jazira under Zufar ibn al-Harith al-Kilabi, who continued to recognize Ibn al-Zubayr's suzerainty'; the Second Fitna page: the Qays 'continued supporting the Zubayrids'.
685: Marwan I and his son Abd al-Aziz retake Egypt.
685: Najda 'established an independent state in Najd and Yamama in 685'; the Najdat page dates his revolt there to 682 and does not say the land was taken from anyone.
Page silent on when: the Najdat 'extended their authority to Bahrain, Oman, and parts of Yemen'.
688/9: Zuhayr ibn Qays retakes Kairouan.

688: 'In 688, the emperor Justinian II and the caliph Abd al-Malik reached an unprecedented agreement'; 'for the next 300 years, Cyprus was ruled jointly by both the Caliphate and the Byzantines as a condominium' and 'The collected taxes were divided between the Arabs and the emperor'.
690: Byzantine landing in Cyrenaica.
691: Abd al-Malik reconquers Iraq.
691: 'In 691, he besieged the Qaysite stronghold of Qarqisiya in the Jazira'.
692: 'At some time before the end of 692, Ibn Khazim was intercepted and killed by Bukayr ibn Wisha al-Sa'di's troops', and Bukayr sent his head to Abd al-Malik; Bukayr succeeded him.
692: Sebastopolis.
692: Ibn al-Zubayr falls.
693: the Najdat 'were eventually defeated by the caliphate in 693, at the battle of Mushahhar'.
Year not on any page: the Maghreb page has Barqa 'fallen out of Muslim control' in 690 and, 'In 694 a new army was sent, taking Carthage'; it never says who recovered Barqa.
695: Hassan ibn al-Nu'man's campaign.
698: Carthage falls.
698: the fighting for Carthage ends with its capture.
698: al-Muhallab defeats Qatari.

698-703: 'For five years Al-Kahina ruled a sovereign Berber state from the Aurès Mountains to the oasis of Ghadames (698-703)'; in 698 she demolished Baghaya, met Hassan in the Meskiana valley and 'defeated Hassan decisively'.
c. 701: the Kahina is defeated. She was 'based in the eastern Aures' and met her defeat 'in a battle around 701'; the page does not give 698 or 703.
705: Qutayba takes Balkh.
705: Arminiya.
708/9: Musa ibn Nusayr conquers Tangier and the Sus; the Maghreb page: 'In 708 after establishing a garrison at Tangier'; 'As late as 736 campaigns were still being sent into the Sus'.
708: infobox 'Annexed by Umayyad Caliphate: 708'.
709: Qutayba storms Bukhara.
709: Bukhara is annexed with an Arab garrison in the citadel.
710: after Nezak's revolt of 709 'Abd al-Rahman retook Tokharistan' in spring and installed a garrison near Balkh; the page dates it only by sequence (710 is the reading).
710: 'The emirate was founded in 710 CE by Salih I ibn Mansur through a Caliphate grant'; infobox 'Client state of the Umayyad Caliphate (710-750)'.
711: Tariq lands.

712: Merida. 'In 712, Tariq's forces were then reinforced by those of his superior' (Musa); Merida was 'ultimately conquered in mid-summer 712'. Cordoba and Toledo were 'stormed and captured unconditionally'.
711-712: Samarkand surrenders to Qutayba.
711-712: Khwarazm surrenders; the Transoxiana page is silent on a Qutayba conquest of Khwarazm.
713: Musa and Tariq meet and 'the following year the combined forces continued... capturing Leon, Astorga and Zaragoza'.
711-713: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim conquers Sindh.
713/14: Maslama recovers Derbent.
714: Musa 'overran the western Basque regions and the Cantabrian mountains all the way to Gallaecia'; Pamplona's submission falls in this period without a date.
714: the main conquest ends.
715: 'Indian kings recaptured most territories after Ibn al-Qasim left in 715' (Alor and Mehran in 715, renewed attacks at Brahmanabad in 718).
716: Yazid ibn al-Muhallab invades.

717: the page is silent on the outcome; the Farrukhan the Great page has Yazid agreeing to withdraw 'in return for tribute' and 'The following year (717), the caliph Umar II had Yazid dismissed and imprisoned'.
717: al-Hurr 'initiat[ed] in 717 the first forays across the Pyrenees into Septimania'.
717: the second siege of Constantinople.
718: the siege is abandoned ('the siege was abandoned on 15 August 718').
720: Narbonne falls.
720: the Turgesh counter-offensive.
721: Toulouse.
721: the Visigothic kingdom ends; Ardo 'died in 721' and Septimania, its last land, is Umayyad (Narbonne 720).
721: 'Hullishah surrendered at Brahmanabad'.
722: the second Arab-Khazar war.
723: Junayd (governor of Sindh from 723) 'conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan'; raids on Ujjain, Mirmad and Dahnaj ran 724-740; in 725 Nagabhata I 'defeated a large Arab force near Avanti'.

723-726: 'Junayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Murri (723-726) recaptured Sindh, conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan'; 'Altogether, Al-Junayd have conquered all of Gujarat, a large part of Rajasthan, and some parts of Madhya Pradesh'; the kingdoms weakened or destroyed include the Maitrakas of Saurashtra, the Kacchelas of…

723-726: the same campaign took 'Mermad (Maru-Mada, in Jaisalmer and Jodhpur)', 'al-Baylaman (Bhillamala or Bhinmal)' and 'Jurz (Gurjaradesa)', destroying 'the Bhattis of Jaisalmer, the Gurjaras of Bhinmal, the Moris of Chittor, the Guhilas of Mewar'.
728: 'Suluk, who in 728 took Bukhara'.
732: 'By 732, two large Arab expeditions to Samarkand managed to restore Caliphal authority there, at heavy cost.
732: the Umayyad advance into Gaul ends with the 'Umayyad defeat at Tours by the Franks'.
734: 'al-Harith ibn Surayj took Balkh and Marv, then defected to the Turgesh'.
737 (winter): al-Harith is beaten at Kharistan by the governor Asad; the zone returns to the Caliphate.
737: Marwan ibn Muhammad's invasion ends the war.
739: 'The Battle of Navsari (739): Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin defeated the Arabs.'
739: the Navsari fight is a single defeat; al-Hakam died in 740 fighting the Maitrakas.
740: 'In 740, Maysara al-Matghari' began the Berber revolt; 'By late 742 they'd annihilated several Arab armies'.
742: the Great Berber Revolt reaches the middle Maghreb.
743: 'Taking advantage of his [Suluk's] death, Nasr recovered most of Transoxiana by 743', 'except for the Ferghana Valley, control over which was lost'.
743: the Turgesh war for Sogdia ends with Nasr's recovery of Transoxiana.
743: 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743.'
743: the Indian campaign ends; the page describes a hiatus from 740 to 750.
743: 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; the Arabs were 'decisively defeated at Navsari in 739'.
744: Marwan II moves the capital to Harran.
744-745: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib assembled a small force in Tunis and declared himself emir of Ifriqiya' (744); the Umayyad governor Handhala 'consented to return to Damascus in February 745'.
747: 'On 9 June 747 (Ramadan 25, 129 AH), Abu Muslim successfully initiated an open revolt against Umayyad rule.'
748: Khorasan is won with the control of Merv on 14 February 748.
748: 'On 14 February 748, he established control of Merv.'
Aug 748: Qahtaba 'defeated a 10,000-strong Umayyad force at the Battle of Jurjan in August and subsequently took Rayy'.
749: 'in March 749 he defeated a larger Umayyad army under Amir ibn Dubara... near Isfahan'; 'Nihavand fell after a short siege and the Abbasid army began moving towards Iraq'.
749: Kufa falls on '2 September 749' and on 'Friday, 28 November 749' al-Saffah (Abu al-Abbas) is recognised as caliph in the mosque of Kufa.
Page silent on the date.

750: Yusuf al-Fihri, governor since January 747, was 'ruling independently following the collapse of the Umayyad Caliphate in 750' and 'ruled as king (malik), and not as governor (wali)' for nine years; Abd al-Rahman beat him at Musarah in March 756.
750: the infobox range of the client status ends in 750; the page does not describe the end of the relation.
750: the Zab ('On 16 January 750' the forces met and Marwan II was defeated 'nine days later') and then 'Damascus fell to the Abbasids in April'.
750: 'In August, he and his family were tracked down and killed in Egypt.'
750: the Umayyad Caliphate ends with the death of Marwan II.

wars.name: First Fitna
wars.outcome: Mu'awiya won: Ali was killed in January 661, Hasan ceded the caliphate and Mu'awiya held the whole of it, with Egypt taken in 658.

wars.name: Second Fitna
wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: the Zubayrid caliphate dissolved with Ibn al-Zubayr's death in October/November 692 and the Marwanids replaced the Sufyanids.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of the Maghreb (Umayyad phase)
wars.outcome: The Byzantines left Africa (Carthage 698), the Kahina fell c.

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: the Visigothic kingdom ended (Ardo died 721), the north was left to the Asturian principality, and the advance stopped at Toulouse (721) and Tours (732).

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Transoxiana (Umayyad phase)
wars.outcome: Qutayba conquered 'the larger part of Transoxiana' in 705-715; the Turgesh took Bukhara in 728, the Arabs restored Samarkand by 732, Nasr recovered 'most of Transoxiana by 743', except the Ferghana Valley.

wars.name: Second Arab-Khazar war
wars.outcome: Stalemate: the Khazars beat the Arabs at Ardabil (730) but Marwan ibn Muhammad's 737 invasion left Derbent 'the northernmost outpost of the Muslim world' and the North Caucasus in Khazar hands.

wars.name: Arab-Byzantine wars (Umayyad period)
wars.outcome: Arab gains in Armenia (692) and Africa (698); both sieges of Constantinople failed (678, 718); the frontier settled on the Taurus-Antitaurus line.

wars.name: Umayyad campaigns in India
wars.outcome: Victory of the Indian kingdoms: 'Umayyad expansion restricted to Sindh' (infobox 711-740).

wars.name: Abbasid Revolution
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: 'Abbasid victory' (9 June 747 - July 750); the Zab was fought in January 750 and Marwan II killed in Egypt in August.

certainty.note: Civil war: which lands each side held is approximate and the Cliopatria shape is largely replaced by 658 and 684 keyframes.
Steppe, desert and Berber frontiers are approximate.
